title: How does De Zerbi fix Spurs' scoring troubles?
description: Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham are yet to score a Premier League goal this season, how do they fix that?
fullText:
Four games into the season, Tottenham Hotspur and Coventry City are the only sides yet to score in the Premier League.

Spurs have brought in £320m worth of talent – a bulk of that in attacking reinforcements – so why are they struggling to score?

We analysed the tactics Roberto de Zerbi is trying to implement and what potential fixes may look like.

While the Premier League looks different to when De Zerbi left Brighton in 2024, the Italian has shown clear signs of adapting while retaining his tactical principles.

De Zerbi's sides entice opponents to apply pressure – often through slowing down play and passing the ball backwards.

They then react to the opponents' movements by speeding up play, looking to take advantage of the spaces behind the pressing players through direct passing or powerful carrying.

In a 2020 coaching seminar, De Zerbi explained: "The stronger the pressure of the opponent, the more vertical [our] action becomes. [The fewer opponents behind], the easier it becomes to go and score."

We have seen De Zerbi's forwards in bigger spaces facing fewer defenders on numerous occasions this season already.

Turning build-up play to goals, however, requires many parts to come together.

Spurs' shape in possession can be hard to read but it often looks like a 2-3-2-3.

The holding midfielder, usually Rodrigo Bentancur, anchors the midfield in front of Spurs' two central defenders with this trio remaining fairly fixed.

The 2-3-2-3 shape generally stays the same but there is rotation between the wingers, full-backs and central midfielders.

In rotating, players are encouraged to maintain the side's shape by swapping zones with their team-mates – filling gaps as they arise.

On top of these positional rules, De Zerbi gives his sides principles to implement.

A lot of what he is doing worked well during his time at Marseille - from 2024 to 2026 - where they averaged 2.3 goals per game.

It might not be happening for De Zerbi yet this season at Tottenham. But they might not be that far off.

De Zerbi encourages his players to play centrally.

When Spurs' centre-backs are on the ball, opposing midfielders and forwards begin to push up, creating space for Spurs' attacking midfielders between the lines.

The other effect this central play has is that it can draw the defending team in-field, which opens up space in the wide areas for Spurs' direct wingers to attack.

When playing these passes into the middle, a few things have to align.

Players receiving the pass have to be comfortable doing so under pressure and naturally, some are more suited to these constraints.

Recognising that Sandro Tonali is better in big space facing forwards, we have seen him rotate positions with Archie Gray, who starts at right-back - a sensible tweak.

Although not his natural position, the 20-year-old has managed in these tight spaces and appears to understand the tactical demands of his manager.

The return of James Maddison, who came back from a shoulder injury for last Tuesday's Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool, will provide De Zerbi with a player better suited to these spaces and in turn help get Spurs into attacking zones more often.

Individual player quality aside, much of the success of this approach will come down to players internalising their manager's instructions.

And it will take time for some of the squad to unlearn the habits they developed under previous coaches.

At the start of last season under Thomas Frank, Spurs built up primarily down the flanks, almost skipping the centre of the pitch entirely. The logic then was to avoid the risk associated with turnovers in the middle of the pitch.

De Zerbi is actively coaching an unorthodox style that goes against these instructions - but getting players to be brave enough to play in congested areas may take some time.

Spurs' build-up has regularly got them in positions behind the opposition midfield by attacking quickly after they are pressed.

Turning these great attacking situations into goals has been one of Spurs' biggest issues.

There are three parts to this. The first is the ability to recognise the best pass available. This depends the second element - the movement of players ahead of them. Thirdly, players need to have the ability to execute the pass.

Spurs' biggest bottleneck so far has been in players either failing to recognise or opting not to play through balls in behind.

The attacking runs, particularly from Omar Marmoush, have generally been good but passes haven't always followed.

Gray has attempted to feed passes down the line but Spurs have not done this regularly more centrally.

Pedro Porro, known for his ability to create chances, took up a more central role in possession for Spain this summer as they won the World Cup.

As he returns, his natural tendencies, which suit these tactics, may help Spurs create more goalscoring chances.

They might then get some of the joy that De Zerbi's forwards had at Marseille.

But while Porro gets up to speed, others in the Tottenham team are still getting to grips with the runs expected of them.

During De Zerbi's time at Marseille, diagonal runs from wide attackers on the last line, found by willing vertical passers, worked as a way of finding goals.

Igor Paixao's goal in Marseille's 2-2 draw with Toulouse last season is a strong example of these ideas working well, with De Zerbi's former club displaying a good understanding of direct passing and well-timed off-ball movement.

Similarly, against Liverpool on Tuesday, we saw Destiny Udogie get into good positions on the left flank.

Although Andy Robertson has played well for Tottenham this season, Udogie's physicality and timing helped him exploit space when the game became stretched.

This allowed Spurs to get into crossing positions against a disorganised Liverpool shape.

When an attacking side accelerate play, it is common for the defending team to drop back in an urgent manner, looking to protect their goal.

When this happens, space opens up in front of the defence, for late-arriving midfielders or clever strikers that drop back.

Again, Marmoush has tried to do this on a number of occasions but has not always been found.

This may be a matter of players requiring time to gel. For Savio, it may also be a wide player struggling to pull the ball back on their weak foot.

Left-footed right-winger Savio is better at getting to the byeline but the left-footed Udogie and Robertson have created clearer chances via crosses.

At Marseille, both right winger and right full-back were comfortable cutting the ball back on their right foot.

These crosses were maximised by the excellent box-movement of 37-year-old Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.

Looking at how De Zerbi is trying to work, it is easier to see how many of Tottenham's attacking moves are almost there in terms of creating clearer chances.

This is not to say things will be perfect immediately. Successful tactics depend on a team's quality - and Marseille's forwards were excellent finishers who thrived in space.

But if the small details across the pitch are refined, Spurs should create enough chances to score, even if they miss a few.

title: Sutton's predictions v legendary guitarist Johnny Marr
description: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on legendary guitarist and Man City fan Johnny Marr, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.
fullText:
The pressure is growing on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, but can his side sign off for the three-week international break by beating Fulham on Sunday?

"For teams who have had a bad start to the season, United being one of them, it could be a horrible few weeks," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.

"Any negativity is going to just fester, really. There will be speculation about his future, along with all the talk about whether this is a good time to replace your manager.

"United are not the only team to have made a bad start, but there is a lot to ponder on for them at the moment. It makes this weekend even more important."

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers and a variety of guests.

For week four, he takes on legendary guitarist and Manchester City fan, Johnny Marr.

Marr's new album, The Age Of Everything, is out on 2 October.

Do you agree with their scores? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competitions.

Marr has enjoyed City's 100% start to the new Premier League season, with Sunday's win at Old Trafford continuing their impressive start under new boss Enzo Maresca.

"I think that derby will be remembered by City fans for a long time," Marr told BBC Sport.

"We all feared the worst when Phil Foden was sent off so early, because you don't know what could happen. It should have been a yellow card for him and Bruno Fernandes anyway.

"It's all a bit of a learning curve for the fans and the club with a new manager and so many new players, so to see how the team dug in and won was so great for City fans.

"No-one expected Maresca to win his first four games... but then again, why not? He's shown that he's his own man with his own philosophy. I like him."

Chris Sutton and Johnny Marr were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

Gtech Community Stadium, 20:00 BST

Chelsea are free-scoring and their front-line is so dynamic - but they are leaking goals left, right and centre and they are a bit of a rabble at the back.

I do think Chelsea will stop conceding eventually, but finding the right balance between defence and attack is Xabi Alonso's big problem at the moment because it is far too easy to create chances against his side.

Brentford boss Keith Andrews has got that balance in his team. They are very dangerous on the counter-attack, so you have to think they will hurt Chelsea too.

This fixture finished in a 2-2 draw in September last year, and I can see it going the same way this time.

Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, 12:30

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi has this reputation of being a great coach, and we saw what a good job he did at Brighton.

But we have not seen any improvement from Spurs yet, despite the big money they have spent, and he is surely going to come under pressure soon if their poor results continue.

They are not the only ones to revamp their squad but if you listen to De Zerbi, after about five years they might come good.

He keeps saying they need time, but he has had long enough for their results to be much better already. Other clubs, like Hull and Ipswich, have brought plenty of players in and are doing well enough - so why aren't Spurs?

I think De Zerbi has to come under scrutiny, but it is different with Unai Emery at Aston Villa.

They are also without a league win, but they look more likely to score goals, as they showed against Coventry in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.

I am expecting Villa to improve the same way they did after not winning any of their first five games last season, and I can see them edging this.

Do I give Spurs their first league goal of the season? Yes, but only one. They are due a deflection, or Villa will score an own goal.

Something will go for them, but not the result.

There might be a bit of an edge to this one after Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler had a pop at Arsenal over their time-wasting when they beat the Seagulls near the end of last season.

I love the way Brighton play and I was at Old Trafford to watch their comeback to beat Manchester United in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.

It doesn't seem to matter who they are missing from their team, Brighton are just bold as brass with the way they press and get men forward.

Luka Vuskovic, who they got from Spurs for £46m in the summer, is only 19 but he strolled through the game against United. What a player he looks.

The issue I have with Brighton in this game, however, is that Arsenal are not Manchester United. They are a cut above that.

Arsenal are the real deal and I don't see any weaknesses in their team, as their impressive win at Sunderland underlined. They are brave going forward, but they are also street-wise defensively and can see out a game when they have to, time-wasting or not.

They have that steel about them but I also think they could expose Brighton if Hurzeler's side go toe-to-toe with them, which is what I am expecting.

I nearly went for an Ipswich draw last week but changed my mind and went for Crystal Palace to win.

That meant I'd predicted Ipswich would lose their first four league games and they are joint-bottom of the table based on my predictions (see bottom of page).

Gary O'Neil's side have obviously done much better than that in reality - I know Palace went down to 10 men last week but, even so, well done to the Tractor Boys for finding a way to win that game.

Fair play to them, I like the ambition the club's owners have shown in the transfer market, and I really like the way O'Neil sets his team up. They are not just there to sit in in games, and they have got their reward.

I still fancy Everton to win this, though. They have made a great start to the season to stay unbeaten so far and, under David Moyes, they are a battle-hardened, resolute and well-organised outfit.

As a former Norwich striker I often get accused of being biased against Ipswich, but I am not being overly negative about them here.

I just see it being a tough afternoon for them, without getting a goal, and then a long trip home for Ipswich fans on the A14 - hopefully they don't close any of the major roads on Saturday so it is not an even more miserable journey back for them.

I can see this being a frustrating afternoon for Newcastle because they are going to come up against a Hull team who are brilliant at defending the box but are also brave with the way they throw people forward.

They are a threat from set-plays too but they have got the bit between their teeth and their whole attitude seems to be 'attack the Premier League' after getting promoted, which I really admire.

Along with Ipswich, Hull are the only other team I've predicted to lose all their games so far.

I am going to tip them not to lose this time... so you know what is probably going to happen. Apologies in advance to Tigers fans, because this happened with me and Sunderland last season.

Coventry were served up a couple of shockers by getting Arsenal and Manchester City as their first two away fixtures and this trip is far from easy for them either.

In fact this is another stinker of a game for Sky Blues boss Frank Lampard, because they are still struggling while Oliver Glasner seems to be getting Nottingham Forest going after a slow burner of a start.

There is a strong chance that Coventry's confidence has been sapped already so Lampard will be trying to rally the troops and give his players some belief that they can compete at this level.

That is going to be really difficult because they must be looking at the results of the other promoted teams and not just thinking 'where is a win coming from for us?' - but also 'where is a point coming from?', and 'where is a goal coming from?' too.

I don't think they will get any of those things this week, because Forest are looking pretty solid.

Well done to Forest striker Liam Delap by the way, who got his first goal for them in last week's win at Aston Villa.

He had a tough time at Chelsea, and I know what that is like, so it is great to see him off the mark for his new club.

My value went down by almost 50% when I left Stamford Bridge - from £10m to £6m - so what has gone on there?

Seriously, though, sometimes you need a change of scene to find your form again and Delap must be feeling a bit freer now he has his first Forest goal.

I am not convinced by Liverpool at all after covering them for Radio 5 Live last week - I thought Fulham were the better side in their 0-0 draw at Anfield.

Andoni Iraola's side did not flow in the final third, certainly not in the way his Bournemouth team did last season.

I don't think the Reds players are quite in sync with what Iraola is asking them to do in terms of their press either, and Fulham played through them with ease at times.

Marco Rose is an attacking manager so if Liverpool don't buck their ideas up then Bournemouth are going to do the same, and Iraola could end up losing on his return to his former club.

The one thing in Iraola's favour is that Bournemouth seem to be finding a way to draw games that they should win, so that is the result I am going with even though though I quite fancy the Cherries to take all three points.

I think I am in love with Leeds boss Daniel Farke. What a guy.

We were talking about him on the Monday Night Club before Leeds walloped Newcastle and only idiots question whether he is the right man to move the club forward now.

To see them beat Newcastle, and how emphatically they did it, was massive and more proof of their progress.

In contrast, Crystal Palace are almost on the precipice after their shaky start under new manager Pierre Sage, and I just don't see the Eagles getting anything here.

Leeds are so well organised at the back with new goalkeeper James Trafford, who is an upgrade on last season, and and a new centre-half I like too, in Tarik Muharemovic.

Apart from me, no-one else could say Muharemovic's name on the Monday Night Club, not even the posh Rory Smith, which I quite enjoyed.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is flying up front, as well. He is fit, motivated and a real handful, which is another reason I can't see past a Leeds victory.

Sunderland are a really good team and, on their day, they are more than a match for anyone.

The Black Cats are strong and robust, and when they get after teams and press you then they are phenomenal.

All of that makes me think this is a really hard game for Manchester City.

Their derby victory was a brilliant win and Maresca's biggest result as their manager so far, with the way they did it.

Iliman Ndiaye showed what a good signing he is when he came on for Rayan Cherki in the second half at Old Trafford, in terms of offering a different profile.

Cherki's more of an inside forward, as a number 10 or playing narrow, and he's a guy where you think you couldn't get the ball off him in a telephone box.

Ndiaye, though, will do more work going back and is also more of a ball carrier, so he was exactly what City needed when they went a man down.

United can feel hard done by because City's winner should have been disallowed, but City were the better team with 10 men.

This will be a very different task for Maresca's men, with the emphasis on them breaking down the Black Cats, but I don't feel it will just be one-way traffic.

I still think City will find a way though, and they need to for the sake of the title race. They already seem to be the only team capable of keeping pace with Arsenal.

Johnny on former boss Pep Guardiola, who stepped down in the summer, and his favourite City players: No-one expected Pep to stay for 10 years so it made him leaving OK to accept, and good luck to him. Aside from the success he brought to the club, City fans loved him because he totally loved Manchester.

Dennis Tueart was my favourite player when I was a kid and I think he could have played in this current era. We've had amazing players in the last 12 or so years so how do you pick, but my favourites would be Vincent Kompany, Sergio Aguero and David Silva, with the top place going to Kevin De Bruyne. I'd say he's the best player I've seen in a City shirt.

Watching Fulham draw at Anfield last weekend changed my view on them.

I had not seen Alvaro Arbeloa's side over 90 minutes before and, while their other results were poor, this time they were excellent.

They cut through Liverpool and had some nice patterns of play, but also defended well too. Arbeloa said afterwards that they played with more balance and I think that is a good way to describe their display.

Then I went to Manchester United's defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, and their performance was very poor.

Carrick really needs a response with a win here to take into the international break but how can I give United a chance, after the way the Seagulls absolutely dismantled them?

Three times in the past four seasons, United have gone to Craven Cottage and nicked the win late on, but I can't make a case for that happening.

As well as having problems up front, United are struggling defensively and I can see Fulham creating plenty of opportunities against them too.

Chris and his guest, Dorking Wanderers boss Marc White, both got four correct results with no exact scores from the 10 games in week four, giving them 40 points each.

AI did better, thanks to an exact score for Brentford's 2-2 draw with Bournemouth which, along with two other correct results, gave it a total of 60 points.

But it was the collective efforts of the BBC readers who took the weekly win - their first of the season - that also sees them move from bottom to level on points with Chris at the top of the predictions table.

They also got one exact score - Arsenal's 2-0 win at Sunderland - but also managed four correct results, giving them a total of 40 points.

It was a tough week for predictions, with only two games where everyone picked the right outcome - that victory for the Gunners, and Brighton's win at Coventry.

There were five games where none of our predictors guessed the result - Nottingham Forest's win at Aston Villa, Hull's draw at Chelsea, Ipswich's win at Crystal Palace, Fulham's draw at Liverpool and Leeds' win over Newcastle.

The biggest shock of the week came at Anfield. From more than 33,000 predictions, just under 30,000 (91%) of you went for a Liverpool win, while fewer than 2,000 of you went for any sort of draw and only 390 of you got the correct 0-0 scoreline.

fullText:
Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner has been speaking to the media before Saturday's Premier League game against Coventry City at the City Ground (kick-off 17:30 BST).

Here are the key lines from his news conference:

Nikola Milenkovic will miss the game, while fellow defender Jair Cunha trained on Thursday and "looks OK", though Glasner added that it was a "very light session".

Glasner described planning approval for the development of the City Ground as "great news for the club, the city and the supporters".

Asked if he expected to still be at the club when the works are complete, he said: "I never think about leaving. You don't start a relationship and think about when you can leave. It makes no sense. I'm always thinking mid- and long-term. If somebody asks me how I see things, I always try to look a little bit outside of football."

On last weekend's win at Aston Villa: "It was good out of possession but it was maximum OK in possession and I would say below average in possession in the first half. Of course, when you win and when you show a good performance it helps in getting more and more belief, getting more and more confidence."

On Morgan Gibbs-White and whether he should receive an England call-up having missed out on the World Cup squad: "I think he showed maximum effort, commitment and good performances. It's Thomas Tuchel's decision."

Glasner said he spent some time with Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis: "Sometimes you are emotional during a game, this is what I talked about to him, because he's also quite emotional. I don't talk to the players after the game. It makes no sense - because then maybe you regret it the following day."

The Austrian said Saturday's opponents Coventry, who are yet to register a point or score a goal in the league, will pose "the same challenges we have faced and will face in every Premier League game". He added: "They are a good team with a fantastic manager. They played a great Championship season. They had quite a tough schedule at the beginning [of this season]."

On the upcoming international break: "We decided to give the players the first week off. It's quite difficult to keep the motivation high when you know there is no competitive game in the mid-season. Then, in the second week, we will start having a normal training week with a friendly game on Saturday. Then, in the third week, hopefully all internationals will come back well without any injuries. Then we prepare for Crystal Palace."

title: Premier League Gameweek 4 Review: Biggest Talking Points and Takeaways
description: The English Premier League Gameweek 4 gave us plenty to talk about, with Arsenal maintaining their perfect start to the season and staying at the top of the table. Some of the other big teams, however, dropped points during another busy weekend of action. Manchester City claimed bragging rights in the Manchester derby with a […]
fullText:
The English Premier League Gameweek 4 gave us plenty to talk about, with Arsenal maintaining their perfect start to the season and staying at the top of the table. Some of the other big teams, however, dropped points during another busy weekend of action.

Manchester City claimed bragging rights in the Manchester derby with a narrow win over Manchester United, while Brighton & Hove Albion and Leeds United picked up impressive victories.

Chelsea were also held by Hull City, adding another surprise result to the weekend.

With four rounds now completed, some teams are starting to make a strong impression while others have raised more questions. There were also standout performances, unexpected results and a few issues that could shape what comes next.

Here are the biggest talking points and takeaways from Gameweek 4:

Arsenal remain one of the most reliable teams for Fantasy Premier League managers after another strong result. Their 2-0 win over Sunderland made it four wins from four, while they also kept another clean sheet.

David Raya was one of the standout performers after saving a penalty, while Bukayo Saka scored from the spot. Arsenal's defence has also continued to look strong, making their defenders and goalkeeper attractive options for managers looking for reliable points.

The same can be said about their attacking players, Arsenal have shown that they can deliver at both ends of the pitch, which makes their key players difficult to overlook as we move into the next few Gameweeks.

Chelsea were unable to beat newly promoted Hull City, but the 2-2 draw should not completely change how FPL managers view their attacking players.

The Blues have shown plenty of potential going forward, and Joao Pedro continued that trend by scoring and providing an assist against Hull City. Their attacking options remain attractive, even though their defensive performances have caused some concern.

For FPL managers, the main question is whether Chelsea can turn their attacking threat into more consistent results. Their next few fixtures should give us a better idea of which players are worth keeping in our plans.

Fabian Hurzeler's men produced one of the biggest results of the weekend by beating Coventry City 5-0. It was a dominant display and naturally put several of their players on the radar.

Pascal Grob was the standout performer, scoring once and providing two assists. Other Brighton players also picked up useful FPL returns, giving managers more options to consider.

However, it is important not to make a transfer simply because a player had one big Gameweek. Brighton's upcoming fixtures, along with each player's role and minutes, should also be considered before making a move.

Morgan Gibbs-White is another player who is starting to attract more attention after Nottingham Forest's 2-1 win over Aston Villa.

The midfielder provided an assist and continued his strong start to the season. His involvement in Forest's attacking play makes him an interesting option for managers looking beyond the most popular midfield picks.

His next few fixtures could make him even more appealing, especially if he continues to play an important role for Nottingham Forest. For now, he is certainly a player worth keeping an eye on.

Liverpool were another team expected to deliver in Gameweek 4, but they could only manage a goalless draw against Fulham.

The result was frustrating for managers who backed their attacking players, particularly with Liverpool playing at home. Their lack of goals also gives FPL managers a reason to look at their options more carefully.

That does not mean Liverpool players should be sold after one disappointing result. However, with other attacking options starting to emerge, their performances in the next few Gameweeks will be important.

Tottenham Hotspur's 0-0 draw with Everton was another frustrating result for FPL managers. Roberto De Zerbi's side have now failed to score in their opening four league matches, which is a major concern for their attacking players.

That makes Tottenham's forwards and midfielders difficult to trust at the moment. Their defence could still offer some value, but managers looking for goals and assists may have better options elsewhere.

Tottenham will need to find a way to improve in front of goal soon. Until that happens, FPL managers may be better off waiting before investing in their attacking players.

Leeds United's 4-1 win over Newcastle United was another result that caught the attention of FPL managers. Their attacking players produced a strong performance, while Newcastle United's defence struggled throughout the game.

The result gives Leeds some interesting options to watch, but managers should still be careful about chasing points after one big performance. Their players will need to show that they can produce regularly before becoming serious FPL targets.

fullText:
Coventry boss Frank Lampard has been speaking to the media before Saturday's Premier League game against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground (kick-off 17:30 BST).

Here are the key lines from his news conference:

Swiss defender Aurele Amenda is likely to be unavailable for Saturday's game after picking up a calf injury during the Carabao Cup loss to Aston Villa. "He will be scanned over the next 24 hours or so," said Lampard, who added that it is a blow as Amenda is a good player who makes an impact on and off the pitch.

It is important to Lampard that Coventry are adaptable with formation: "You have a look at the opposition and you see what you feel is the best opportunity to try to get the best out of our team."

Lampard reflected on his side's 3-1 defeat by Villa: "The critical part of the game was set pieces which we gave away. I thought we competed well in phases of the game and specifically the first half and the reaction to going 1-0 down. [We] scored a great, great goal, pushed and created a really good atmosphere in the stadium. Critical things we have to get right."

On club captain Matt Grimes: "He is a great professional, great around team-mates, calm head, very good player. Played a lot of years in the Championship, was very experienced at it and can play for me at any level and now he is integral to everything we do here as a person and as a player."

Lampard said the extended international break is positive in some part as it will allow players who are injured or arrived late in the window to get fit with more training time. But, it means he does not have a complete squad: "It's just one we will manage physically but I think the opportunity to get players fit is a good thing for us."

When asked about keeping up the positive momentum from last season's promotion, he said: "We just have to because it is football. We have been privileged for a while to win a lot of football matches here. It is more difficult when you don't [win], that makes the job of all of ours tougher because that is what we are here for and what you want to do and sometimes it is human nature to feel down but we just have to focus on the work that we have got to do to keep trying to improve, to keep trying to get results."

On Nottingham Forest: "They've got a high-quality squad, we have to be careful. Always good in transition, always good to play vertical and play forward and really talented people between lines, it's a really good system with players that [Oliver Glasner] has got there that suit the system that he is playing, hence it will be a tough match."

title: Ranking the greatest all-time fantasy football icons
description: There's nothing quite like the satisfaction of unearthing an absolute Fantasy Premier League bargain - so who are the most iconic picks ever?
fullText:
Scanning the newspaper, inky fingers and fuzzled minds, scrambling for the calculator and jotting down the codes for Julian Dicks and Juninho. These lads will carry the team until you remember to pick up the house phone and cash in a transfer a few months down the line.

Before templates and triple captains there was a world of fantasy football that existed by writing out your XI and ringing in the names. Parents used it as a summer-holiday maths lesson.

Yet whether in print or online, there's nothing quite like the satisfaction of unearthing an absolute bargain. That free-kick taking defender, the undervalued forward, out-of-position goal-getter or cheap keeper posting clean sheets.

Since it began for the 2002-03 season, Fantasy Premier League has evolved into a huge database boasting millions of players across the globe, with substitutions and wildcards and the maths done for you.

But who, over the past quarter of a century of the competition's official game, are the biggest icons of all time?

With the help of our resident FPL expert Thomas Woods and some extensive research by the Fantasy Football Scout, that's what I'm digging into this week.

Based on stats and a touch of sentiment - Michu, we see you - I've ranked my top 10 below. We'd love to hear your thoughts in the comments, too.

Firstly, let's look at what makes a player iconic. Is it purely posting massive numbers? Thierry Henry's total from the inaugural season, for example, still ranks seventh overall. Indeed the Arsenal man was top scorer in three of the first four campaigns, but also the most expensive.

Frank Lampard, arriving late in the box, topped the charts three times with his goals from midfield for Chelsea, while the twinkle-toed Cristiano Ronaldo did it twice at Manchester United. The pair rank fourth and fifth for best individual seasons, respectively.

It's tempting to say we should discount such "obvious" picks for this debate, but then there's Mo Salah. The Liverpool asset might have eaten up a decent chunk of your budget, but packed guaranteed points for those premium pounds.

As the Fantasy Football Scout explains, since the game began, 52 players have reached 200 points in a season at least once. Salah has done it eight times. And the Egyptian is the only player to ever top 300 points. In fact, he's done it twice.

So Mo probably deserves a go. But we're really searching for those who have offered the most value over the years - cheap picks who seriously delivered.

Some went on to become Premier League stars, others became cult heroes, one-season wonders or bargain buys who got virtual tongues wagging.

10. Harry Kane, Tottenham, 2014-15, starting price £5m

England captain and record goalscorer, three-time Premier League Golden Boot winner. Harry Kane was hardly a secret at Tottenham, right?

After a series of loans and having not yet established himself at White Hart Lane, the young Spurs striker began the 2014-15 campaign as a likely £5m back-up to Emmanuel Adebayor and Roberto Soldado.

Kane didn't find the net until November in the Premier League, a 90th-minute winner after coming off the bench at Aston Villa, but it was the first of 21 goals in the competition that season as the homegrown striker established himself in Mauricio Pochettino's side.

As the Fantasy Football Scout notes, an eight-match run from gameweek 18 to 25 saw Kane notch 77 points with nine goals, four assists and 16 bonus points.

For those who gambled on him early, Kane proved a bargain. He rose from £5m to a peak £6.4m, racking up 191 points and ranking 11th on the all-time value list, despite playing fewer minutes than all those above him.

9. Charlie Adam, Blackpool, 2010-11, £5m.

The great budget enabler. Blackpool's Charlie Adam took penalties, free-kicks, corners and would probably have had goalkicks too if they let him.

He'd had a good season in the Championship, scoring 16 times, but no one really gave the Seasiders any hope on their Premier League debut and thus there was little expectation on the Scottish midfielder from FPL bosses.

Despite Ian Holloway's outfit eventually succumbing to the drop, Adam delivered a points tally that was only bettered by Manchester United's Nani that season - on the back of 12 goals, his 192 stood as the highest score by a promoted player at the time.

8. Michel Vorm, Swansea, 2011-12, £4m

Michel Vorm conceded four goals on his Premier League debut. That stacks up for a £4m keeper, you might think. Yet the Dutchman made 11 saves that day at Manchester City, more than anyone else would manage in a single game that season.

Vorm swept Swansea City's end-of-term awards but also became a FPL legend in the process. He made saves but also kept clean sheets, 14 of them in total, and earned the second-most points for a goalkeeper behind City's Joe Hart, who started the game £3m more expensive.

The Dutchman peaked in price at £5.3m and was the fourth-most owned player in the game at one point. Both virtually and in real life, it would be his standout season.

7. Stuart Dallas, Leeds, 2020-21, £4.5m

Under Marcelo Bielsa, Stuart Dallas was a FPL dream.

Racking up defensive clean sheets while operating further forward than his listed position suggested, cheap as you like, and even doing it against league heavyweights Manchester City, where he scored twice for 17 points.

"The Northern Ireland international's versatility played into the hands of FPL managers because, even though he was a classified as a defender, he played all over the place for Leeds in 2000-21 - more often than not as an attacking midfielder," explains Woods.

"And for a starting price of £4.5m you got eight goals, 12 clean sheets, three assists and a total of 171 points. Bargain."

6. Michail Antonio, West Ham, 2019-20, £7m

Michail Antonio is a curious pick, but deserves FPL cult hero status for one of the most memorable months in the game's history.

Classified as a midfielder but deployed up front, Antonio's value actually dropped during a campaign that was disrupted by injury and the coronavirus pandemic.

Following the restart, Antonio was unstoppable. He played seven times in July 2020, scoring eight goals. Incredibly, four of those came in West Ham's 4-0 away win at Norwich, where the midfielder posted a 26-point haul.

That's the joint-most on record for a player valued under £7m, alongside Cole Palmer, and only three off Salah's overall record for a single gameweek.

5. John Lundstram, Sheffield United, 2019-20, £4m

Lord Lundstram, as he was fondly known, didn't notch a season total as high as some on this list, but his bargain price, out-of-position listing and the fact he seemingly appeared from nowhere, having only made five starts for the Blades the previous season, saw him achieve legendary status in FPL.

"A £4m defender is usually the last spot on FPL managers' benches but Lundstram was misclassified by FPL towers and was actually a box-to-box midfielder," says Woods.

"He scored five goals and delivered four assists while picking up clean sheets along the way to 144 points, with his two-goal 21-point haul in week 11 particularly memorable.

"And being able to start a £4m asset allowed managers to cram more talent into the rest of the team too."

4. Riyad Mahrez, Leicester, 2015-16, £5.5m

Riyad Mahrez was a goldmine for Claudio Ranieri and FPL bosses alike during Leicester's title-winning season. As the Fantasy Football Scout notes, he flew out of the blocks with a 15-point haul in week one against Sunderland, rewarding the 5.9% of managers who started the season with the winger in their side.

It was no fluke. Mahrez made double figures in five of the opening six gameweeks, his 56 points among the best starts ever to a FPL campaign. Inevitably, other managers jumped on board, and by week seven Mahrez was in more than 50% of teams.

Jamie Vardy, of course, had a dazzling season of his own, returning a goal or an assist for 15 weeks on the bounce, though he started £0.5m more expensive than his team-mate.

Mahrez finished the campaign as the top scorer in FPL with 240 points, despite his modest starting price.

3. Michu, Swansea, 2012-13, £6.5m

Of course, there is a certain amount of nostalgia and sentiment to FPL. We gaze proudly at these little icons clocking up points like they're family.

Michu was the epitome of an on-screen cult hero, going from relative unknown to bagging 190 points, his price rising by £2m throughout the year.

As Woods says, he is probably the biggest one-season wonder in FPL history.

"A few savvy managers picked up on the fact the Spaniard had scored 15 goals in La Liga the season before and had him on the opening day when he scored twice at QPR," adds our resident FPL expert.

"He was effectively a £6.5m striker classified as a midfielder. It felt like he was in most managers' teams by the time he ended 2012-13 with a whopping 18 goals.

"He managed two the following season... and then left for Napoli."

2. Mohamed Salah, Liverpool, 2024-25, £12.5m

OK, firstly, other Liverpool assets were perhaps unfortunate to miss out on this list - flying full-backs Trent Alexander-Arnold and Andy Robertson were consistently must-have picks.

Luis Suarez, meanwhile, boasts the third-highest score ever and, as the Fantasy Football Scout points out, he notched a record 55 attacking returns in 2013-14 despite missing the first five games.

But if we can allow one premium pick, it has to be Salah. And if we have to pick a season, it must be his record-breaking 2024-25 campaign when the Egyptian produced a staggering 344 points.

Remarkably, it came off the back of his lowest score the year before - although low for Mo was still upwards of 200 points. Salah, simply, is FPL royalty.

1. Cole Palmer, Chelsea, 2023-24, £5m

You have to put Cole Palmer's 2023-24 season into context. He wasn't a household name, like now, having left Manchester City for more gametime at Chelsea.

The youngster began the season as a £5m midfielder and did not start a game for the Blues until matchweek seven. In fact, as the Fantasy Football Scout explains, only 63,575 managers owned him (0.6%) for his first double-figure return at Burnley the following week.

That crept up to 4.5% for his next 12-pointer at Tottenham in gameweek 12, which then triggered a surge in popularity as FPL bosses lumped on Stamford Bridge's new star.

More than five million owned Palmer when he scored four goals against Everton during a 26-point haul in gameweek 33, albeit he still only cost £6.1m.

"Based on starting price, Cole Palmer in 2023-24 is the best-ever value player in Fantasy," concludes the Scout.

Palmer finished as the season's top scorer with 244 points and was handed the biggest price rise in FPL history of £5.5m, meaning he cost £10.5m at the start of the 2024-25 campaign.

title: Liverpool have a new transfer priority that they cannot ignore
description: Liverpool were expected to completely transform their team in the summer transfer window. Arne Slot led his men to a fifth-place finish last term which, just a year after winning the Premier League ti...
fullText:
Liverpool were expected to completely transform their team in the summer transfer window.

Arne Slot led his men to a fifth-place finish last term which, just a year after winning the Premier League title, was a massive fall from grace.

This lack of form was one of the main reasons why Andoni Iraola was brought in and plenty of change was expected.

And, even though many deals were made, it still feels like more could be done to help improve the Anfield outfit even more.

The Reds are still unbeaten across all competitions at the moment but, as the season has gone on, a new transfer priority seems to have emerged ahead of the next transfer window.

Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas were supposed to share the role of being Liverpool's left-back's this season.

Andy Robertson's contract expired which meant that Kerkez was bumped up to first choice and, like most of Tsimikas' Liverpool career, he was expected to back the Hungarian up if and when needed.

However, now that they have both featured in a few games, it's become clear that neither of them are worthy of being the Reds' starting left-back.

Each of them have terrible decision making skills and, even when the Greek Scouser was given the chance to try and prove his worth for Liverpool in their recent game against Fulham, he ended up getting hooked at half-time due to how badly he played.

Indeed, Kerkez is a better player than Tsimikas with fans thinking that, after spending £45 million on him last summer that Liverpool's left-back would be locked down for years to come.

But, if these recent performance are anything to go by, that is far from the case and, the interest that they showed in some left-wingers during the summer needs to be reignited as a matter of urgency.

Obviously, there were many full-backs linked with Liverpool over the summer.

Djed Spence, Jorrel Hato, Antonee Robinson and Daniel Svensson are just a few examples.

And, while some new rumours have started to emerge about the future of Alejandro Balde, it feels like Svensson could be the perfect option for Liverpool top explore.

A lot of the links with left-backs were dependent on whether Tsimikas was going to leave or not as, even last season, Slot tried to make Kerkez his starting left-back.

However, with how badly both left-backs have performed for Liverpool this term, the £35 million deal for Borussia Dortmund's Svensson actually looks appealing.

He's got plenty of Champions League experience under his belt alongside a decent chunk of Bundesliga outings as well.

Obviously, the Reds would have to change their transfer strategy again and potentially miss out on signing someone such as Lamine Camara but, with how much of a problem area left-back is for them at the moment, it feels like that needs to take priority.

title: A team in form - how Farke has turned Leeds around
description: With Leeds United third in the Premier League, BBC Sport assesses their improvement under Daniel Farke.
fullText:
As the nascent Premier League table takes shape, the sight of Leeds United in third place feels like a throwback to the turn of the century, when they secured five top-five finishes on the bounce.

Monday's 4-1 home win over Newcastle United means Daniel Farke's unbeaten side have made their best start to a top-flight season since 2001-02 under David O'Leary.

In truth, Leeds, with eight points from four games, have been playing well for some time, and it can all be traced back to a bold change of formation by Farke almost nine months ago.

The German switched from a back four to a back three at half-time against Manchester City on 29 November, a game in which his team battled back from 2-0 down at the break to level things at 2-2 before conceding in stoppage time at Etihad Stadium.

Starting with the subsequent home win over Chelsea on 3 December, Leeds have lost only five of their past 29 league games, results which would place them fifth in the hypothetical league table for that timeframe.

So how have they done it? And can they push for European football for the first time in 24 years?

In the 2025 summer transfer window Farke and the club's new sporting director Adam Underwood made a point of signing tall players who could "add a special physicality" to the squad they were building for the robust demands of the English top flight.

Of the 10 permanent arrivals, eight – Jaka Bijol, Sebastiaan Bornauw, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, James Justin, Lukas Nmecha, Noah Okafor, Lucas Perri and Anton Stach – stand more than 6ft tall.

Speaking in July 2025, Farke said: "I wouldn't say it's coincidence that they are all tall players but, of course, if you join the Premier League and you have one of the smallest groups, you expect that probably there is more pressure on you than there was in the Championship. You have to make sure that you're also good in defending crosses."

This summer, after losing centre-back Pascal Struijk to Brighton, Farke moved for two World Cup players - Bosnia-Herzegovina's Tarik Muharemovic and Switzerland's Nico Elvedi - to bolster his defence.

Despite an error leading to Bazoumana Toure's late consolation goal for Newcastle, Muharemovic has looked particularly impressive, playing every league minute in front of 6ft 5in England international James Trafford, who became the most expensive British goalkeeper in history for the second time when he joined for an initial £40m from City.

Throw in Harry Wilson, one of the league's standout players last season, who joined on a free transfer from Fulham, and Leeds' latest signings look to be particularly shrewd.

Leeds lost eight of their first 13 league games in 2025-26, leaving them in 18th position and facing the very real prospect of relegation.

Reports at the time suggested Farke, whose side had pipped Burnley to the Championship title the previous season, was in real danger of losing his job.

While the rejig clearly had its intended effect on the Leeds defence – among the ever-present clubs in the division, only champions Arsenal, City and Nottingham Forest have conceded fewer goals since the switch – it has helped in other areas too.

The most notable beneficiary has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Since last December only Erling Haaland, Ollie Watkins and Joao Pedro have scored more top-flight goals than Calvert-Lewin's 14.

Having toiled as the lone centre-forward in a 4-3-3 formation, relying on infrequent support from out wide, Calvert-Lewin has thrived with a proper strike partner, often in the form of Nmecha or Okafor, who boasts seven goals and an assist in his past 11 league appearances.

Although Farke still finds himself alternating between 3-4-3 and 3-5-2, Calvert-Lewin himself has said: "I enjoy having bodies around me."

With Crystal Palace the visitors to Elland Road on Saturday, Calvert-Lewin is aiming to become the first Leeds player to score in six consecutive league home games since Arthur Hydes in 1932.

The former Everton forward missed out on a place in England's World Cup squad but, with three goals in all competitions this season, he is surely in with a chance of an international recall on Friday as Thomas Tuchel prepares for the Nations League quadruple-header.

Elland Road was bouncing on Monday night as the vast majority of the 36,693 fans savoured Leeds' stunning performance.

The famous old ground has been something of a fortress under the lights in recent seasons. Before consecutive losses to City and Sunderland in February, Leeds had gone 25 evening kick-offs in league and play-off games without a home defeat, winning 20 and drawing five.

The thumping win over Newcastle meant their new manager, Matthias Jaissle, became the latest coach to be welcomed to what Leeds fans call 'Daniel Farke Penitentiary'.

The online meme – in which managers defeated by Farke are 'sentenced' to time in his fictional prison – flooded social media again after the game.

Farke enjoyed the adulation of the supporters at full-time and, while he has quite rightly played down early talk of European qualification, a continuation of this form will have the Elland Road faithful dreaming of a return to those famous Champions League nights of a quarter of a century ago.

title: Ausilio closing in on agreement with Tottenham after 28 years with Inter
description: Multiple outlets in Italy are reporting that former Inter director Piero Ausilio is closing in on an agreement to take over as the new sporting director at Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur after ...
fullText:
Multiple outlets in Italy are reporting that former Inter director Piero Ausilio is closing in on an agreement to take over as the new sporting director at Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur after his 28-year career with the Nerazzurri.

Ausilio officially left his position as sporting director at Inter on September 2, the day after the summer transfer window had come to an end and has since been replaced by his long-term deputy Dario Baccin.

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 17: (L-R) vice Sportif director Dario Baccin, director Piero Ausilio, President Giuseppe Marotta, coach Cristian Chivu and Vice President Javier Zanetti pose for a photo with the Coppa Campioni d'Italia and Coppa Italia trophies following the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Hellas Verona FC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 17, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Ausilio had originally joined Inter as a secretary with the youth teams all the way back in the late 1990s before progressing through various roles and eventually into the position of sporting director, a role that he held for well over a decade.

The Nerazzurri won three Serie A titles, three Coppa Italias and three trophies in the Supercoppa Italiana as well as reaching the Champions League final twice and the Europa League final once.

Reports over the weekend suggested that Ausilio had been approached by Tottenham to take over as sporting director following the end of his time in San Siro.

CAGLIARI, ITALY – AUGUST 28: Piero Ausilio sporting director of Inter looks on during the Serie A TIM match between Cagliari Calcio and FC Internazionale at Sardegna Arena on August 28, 2023 in Cagliari, Italy. (Photo by Enrico Locci/Getty Images)

Now, according to reports from various outlets in Italy including La Gazzetta dello Sport, Ausilio is closing in on an agreement with Tottenham. The Pink Papers claims that it is looking like a matter of 'when' and not 'if' Ausilio goes to Spurs.

He would find several Italian connections in North London, most obviously head coach Roberto De Zerbi and players Sandro Tonali and Destiny Udogie.

Ausilio would also be the second Italian sporting director at Tottenham following the tenure of Fabio Paratici, who is now at the helm at Fiorentina.

title: O'Neill and Graham retain places in NI squad
description: Premier League teenagers Ceadach O'Neill and Braiden Graham keep their places in Northern Ireland's squad for the upcoming Nations League quadruple-header.
fullText:
Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill and Everton's Braiden Graham have kept their places in Northern Ireland's squad for the upcoming Nations League quadruple-header.

The teenage pair were called up for the first time by Michael O'Neill for June friendlies against Guinea and France, with the Arsenal 18-year-old appearing in both games.

Defenders Dan Ballard, Paddy McNair, Terry Devlin and Eoin Toal have all returned to the squad after missing the June games.

Also back after not featuring in the summer are goalkeepers Bailey Peacock-Farrell and Conor Hazard, as well as striker Dion Charles.

There is a place in the squad for Michael Forbes too. The Dundee United defender won his only previous cap against Finland in 2023.

Goalkeepers: Pierce Charles, Conor Hazard, Bailey Peacock-Farrell.

Defenders: Tom Atcheson, Ruairi McConville, Trai Hume, Ciaron Brown, Brodie Spencer, Dan Ballard, Paddy McNair, Eoin Toal, Terry Devlin, Michael Forbes.

Midfielders: Jordan Thompson, Shea Charles, Jamie McDonnell, Justin Devenny, Paul Smyth, Isaac Price, Patrick Kelly, Ethan Galbraith, Kieran Morrison.

Forwards: Josh Magennis, Jamie Donley, Dion Charles, Callum Marshall, Ceadach O'Neill, Braiden Graham.

Liverpool full-back Conor Bradley, who has not played since January after knee surgery, remains absent and has been joined on the sidelines by Preston North End midfielder Ali McCann and Aberdeen's Brad Lyons.

After promotion from the third tier last year, Northern Ireland start their 2026 Nations League B campaign with an away trip to Georgia on 25 September and conclude the window at home to the same opposition on 5 October.

In between they face Hungary in Belfast and Ukraine in Slovakia.

With four games in just an 11-day span, Michael O'Neill has called up 28 players after only selecting 23 for the previous window in June.

The manager also has goalkeepers Luke Southwood and Josh Clarke, along with striker Jamie Reid on standby.

title: No weekend game for Manchester derby VAR officials
description: The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, are not appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.
fullText:
The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, have not been appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.

The decision was made by the Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer Howard Webb and the management team.

It follows Pro Ref admitting to an "error of judgement" in awarding Erling Haaland's winning goal for Manchester City at Manchester United on Sunday.

The striker scored in the 60th minute at Old Trafford when he turned in a shot at the back post from Josko Gvardiol's cross.

His effort was initially disallowed on the field for offside but, following VAR intervention, the goal was awarded as the Norwegian was ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu's boot.

However, there was debate as to whether the goal should have been disallowed for City midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, interfering with play as he dived attempting to head the ball in a central position before Haaland's finish.

"It was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective," said Pro Ref in a statement.

"However, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review."

City, who had Phil Foden sent off after 23 minutes, maintained their 100% league record from four games with the victory.

title: Calvert-Lewin stars but Botman struggles - player ratings for Leeds v Newcastle
description: How Leeds United and Newcastle United's players rated following their Premier League match.
fullText:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin wreaked havoc as Leeds United moved up to third place in the Premier League table following a 4-1 win against Newcastle United at Elland Road.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

James Trafford: A relatively comfortable night against his former suitors. A couple of nervy clearances early on but went on to make an important save to deny Harvey Barnes. 7

James Justin: Teasing cross set up Leeds' second goal. Has become a key component in this system. 7

Nico Elvedi: Only his second Premier League start yet already looks at home at Elland Road. Solid at the back but got it all wrong at the other end after volleying wide at the back post when unmarked. 7

Tarik Muharemovic: The club's player of the month for August for a reason. Made it look rather comfortable at the back on Monday night. 7

Jayden Bogle: Second goal credited to him. Did not know much about it, but has found his shooting boots after his goal at Brighton last time out in the league. Twice forced Lukas Hornicek into big saves before second goal took final touch off him. A real threat. 8

Anton Stach: Won a corner inside 32 seconds. That set the tone for Leeds' relentless display, even if he later wasted chance to score. 7

Ethan Ampadu: Ensured Leeds kept pushing for more as he barked instructions. Saw Dominic Calvert-Lewin inadvertently block a vicious goalbound effort. 7

Ao Tanaka: His goal took two heavy deflections but had the confidence to take the shot. Looking back to his best in recent weeks even if he was relieved to see one misplaced pass unpunished. 7

Gabriel Gudmundsson: Caused Newcastle real problems with his runs down the left. Looked more a winger than a wing-back. 7

Noah Okafor: Fine strike for Leeds' fourth, having also coolly pulled the ball back for Tanaka to let fly for his side's opener. 8

Dominic Calvert-Lewin: Just loves this fixture. A trademark header came off Bogle for Leeds' second and then showed other side of his game to finish calmly on the floor for the hosts' third. Has scored eight goals against Newcastle - more than any other side. 9

Melvin Bard (on 72, Gudmundsson): Perfect environment to make his Premier League debut. 6

Brenden Aaronson (on 72, Tanaka): Lots of energy. 6

Harry Wilson (on 72, Okafor): Eager to impress. 6

Lukas Nmecha (on 78, Calvert-Lewin): 6

Subs not used: Zetterer, Bijol, Bahoya, Nmecha

Lukas Hornicek: This would have been even uglier for the visitors were it not for Hornicek making fine saves to twice deny Bogle and also to foil Calvert-Lewin. 6

Amar Dedic: Shook off hamstring issue to start, but a tough night as Leeds repeatedly targeted his flank. 4

Malick Thiaw: Captain for night but this was far from a captain's performance. Beaten easily by Calvert-Lewin for Leeds' second goal, slapped turf in frustration after the striker fired past him for the third and then failed to block Okafor's fourth. 3

Sven Botman: Like Thiaw, could not cope with Calvert-Lewin and was skinned so easily for Leeds' second goal. 3

Lewis Hall: Dragged out of position in build-up of Leeds' second goal. Not the night he had in mind after signing a new deal. 4

Nico Gonzalez: Belatedly came off after just 19 minutes after the ball struck him in the head in the early stages. 5

Lewis Miley: Little he could do for deflection for Tanaka's goal, but was overrawed by Leeds' tenacious midfield. Had little time to find passing rhythm. 4

Jacob Murphy: Continued in injured Anthony Elanga's absence, but did not offer enough protection and caused Leeds few problems going the other way. 3

Yoane Wissa: Created Newcastle's best chance and at least battled and chased, even if his final ball was not always great. 5

Harvey Barnes: Has a fearsome record against Leeds and eyes lit up when he danced inside the box only for Trafford to deny him. 5

Matias Fernandez-Pardo: Full debut following his £51.4m move from Lille. Had little to feed off as Newcastle repeatedly played long balls forward. 4

Sean Steur (on 19, Gonzalez): Thrown into the cauldron after Gonzalez went off. Could do little about deflection before Leeds' first goal but gave the ball away in build up to Leeds' second. Eighteen-year-old will learn from experience. 4

Bazoumana Toure (on 58, Murphy) So rapid and pulled one back. Bright cameo as he pushes for a start. 6

Joe Willock (on 58, Fernandez-Pardo): One decent chance landed on roof of net from tight angle. 5

Tino Livramento (on 58, Dedic): Another step on return from injury. Set up Toure's consolation. 6

Aladji Bamba (on 79, Miley): A rare sighting following his summer move from Monaco. 5

title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
description: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
fullText:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Gianluigi Donnarumma (Manchester City): Not only is he one of the best goalkeepers in the world, but he is a big-match player. We've seen it year on year and he's just won Manchester City two extra points against Manchester United. He'll get them 10 points over the course of the season, he's that good. After the Community Shield, people were saying he wasn't good enough and they should have kept James Trafford, but he proved again why he's such a big-time goalkeeper.

Daniel Munoz (Nottingham Forest): I thought he was a breath of fresh air in the win at Villa. No-one in that Forest team can do what he does. Pace, power, he can defend and offers you a lot going forward. I thought he was a steal. I can't believe Liverpool and Manchester United didn't go for him. Forest did unbelievable business getting him.

Ezri Konsa (Arsenal): Had a tough old battle against Brian Brobbey as they beat Sunderland. Last season, he ended up bullying Gabriel for the equaliser and he wanted no part of it. Konsa said 'no problem' and stepped up. That penalty was never a penalty.

Lewis Dunk (Brighton): Who knew the big 6ft 5in centre-half could put one in to the top bins, straight off the crossbar? Unbelievable. He goes in just for that strike against Coventry alone.

Tarik Muharemovic (Leeds United): What a beast he is. I don't know where Leeds found him but he heads it, kicks it, runs through people. Didn't get the clean sheet against Newcastle but deserved it.

Leif Davis (Ipswich Town): Very, very good. Very underrated. He delivered in a six-pointer because I think Palace are going to be down there, with a goal and an assist.

Enzo Fernandez (Manchester City): He had his best game in the last two years against Manchester United. He actually did everything the team needed - ran with the ball, looked after it, bought fouls, tried his best to get others sent off. I thought he was a catalyst for the team. His best performance for City so far.

Pascal Gross (Brighton): Goal and assists. The old head who they brought back steadies that ship - it's a really young team. He is even more important now with no Welbeck, no Milner. He is in and is a steady hand.

title: No weekend game for Manchester derby VAR officials
description: The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, are not appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.
fullText:
The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, have not been appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.

The decision was made by the Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer Howard Webb and the management team.

It follows Pro Ref admitting to an "error of judgement" in awarding Erling Haaland's winning goal for Manchester City at Manchester United on Sunday.

The striker scored in the 60th minute at Old Trafford when he turned in a shot at the back post from Josko Gvardiol's cross.

His effort was initially disallowed on the field for offside but, following VAR intervention, the goal was awarded as the Norwegian was ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu's boot.

However, there was debate as to whether the goal should have been disallowed for City midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, interfering with play as he dived attempting to head the ball in a central position before Haaland's finish.

"It was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective," said Pro Ref in a statement.

"However, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review."

City, who had Phil Foden sent off after 23 minutes, maintained their 100% league record from four games with the victory.

title: Familiar questions for Man Utd, now Carrick must find answers
description: After one win in four Premier League games, the problems are mounting for Manchester United and manager Michael Carrick.
fullText:
For the third time in less than 10 months, Manchester United have been beaten by opponents reduced to 10 men before half-time.

While the arguments raging around the 1-0 home defeat by Manchester City have centred around the official apology from Pro Ref to United for what they say was "an error of judgement" around Erling Haaland's matchwinner, the inquest will go much deeper at the club's Carrington training ground.

After pushing back on the idea four points from three games wasn't a great start at Everton last weekend, head coach Michael Carrick now accepts "there is no getting away" from the fact four points from four games is below expectations.

One win, at home to newly-promoted Ipswich, means so many questions - around recruitment, team selection, substitutions, tactics and Carrick himself - will now start to be asked ahead of a huge week.

"We don't need a break or a restart," said Carrick. "We've just got to move on and get winning again."

United entertain Brighton in the Carabao Cup on 16 September, before a trip to Fulham four days later.

If nothing else, Carrick needs his side to deliver to prevent a new three-week international break being filled with external inquests around what is going wrong at Old Trafford.

Speaking in his press conference after the game, new City boss Enzo Maresca accepted Phil Foden's red card made the game more difficult for his side.

However, he also highlighted why he knew it would also be a problem for United.

"They are a team that loves transitions and space in behind," he said.

"With 10 players, we just dropped and waited for them, so we didn't concede any transitions and didn't concede any space in behind. That is why the game became more difficult for us and for them."

United have been more effective as a counter-attacking team since Jose Mourinho arrived at the club over a decade ago. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer wanted to change it, but never quite got there.

The same, to an extent, is true of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, both of whom came to United after achieving success in a domestic league where their side dominated the opposition. As a player, Carrick liked to get on the ball and not give it away. It is fair to assume that is what he wants from his players.

Keeping the ball is one thing. Having the vision and skill to keep possession and create chances against opponents quite prepared to sit in, deny space and keep their shape is another.

United's summer recruitment strategy was based around their midfield. Yet, with Youri Tielemans yet to find top form, Carlos Baleba still to make his debut and Andrey Santos dropped to the bench after the opening game at Hull and not used at all against City, the overall impact of their £155m summer spend has been limited.

At the same time, with Luke Shaw's 41-game run of consecutive Premier League starts coming to an end, there was no fresh back-up at left-back, as most observers expected.

And the introduction of Netherlands forward Joshua Zirkzee – someone who had been available for transfer all summer – for Marcus Rashford seven minutes from time as one of only two United substitutes, gave a strong indication the overall depth in Carrick's squad is not at the level required.

Bruno Fernandes won the PFA and Football Writers' Player of the Year awards last season for an outstanding campaign when he scored nine goals and claimed a Premier League record 22 assists.

So far this season, he has scored three times and has one assist. The goals record is good, but the assists are not. More importantly, his overall impact seems to have dipped.

Some observers felt he looked tired against City, which only heightened questions around his involvement against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK in the Champions League.

Despite their lowly ranking, it was understandable why Carrick would take no chances with his team selection as United returned to Europe's elite competition after a two-year absence.

However, with his side three goals up at the break and knowing there was a three-day turnaround to the City game, it was puzzling why Carrick elected to leave his skipper on the pitch for the full 90 minutes as he chose to use all five substitutes.

Now into the final year of his contract, which United have the option to extend to the summer of 2028, a continued over-reliance on Fernandes is a concern.

Carrick was appointed head coach on a permanent basis with a two-year contract in May after presiding over 12 victories in 17 games when in temporary charge following Amorim's dismissal.

While most said Carrick deserved his shot at the job full-time, others said it smacked of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's appointment, also after impressing in interim charge in 2019.

Solskjaer's record is decent and he remains the only United boss from the post Sir Alex Ferguson era to deliver successive top three finishes.

Yet the Norwegian never shrugged off claims he was not an elite coach. Critics will continue to argue the same is true of Carrick until he proves them otherwise.

When City were reduced to 10 men, did he go for the jugular?

"I thought we had a fair bit of the initiative, especially second half," he said. "Before they scored, I thought we were better.

"I thought we could improve on the second half of the first half. I thought we'd come out at half-time and build momentum. We hit the post, and the game was building the way we wanted. Then the goal obviously had a big impact.

"We could have finished the game better. We could have been a little bit more creative."

No-one is panicking just yet, but United's start to the season has raised familiar questions. Carrick needs to find the answers.

title: Is the Premier League already a two-team title race?
description: Four games is far too soon to be talking about who is in or out of the title race... isn't it? BBC Sport asks if this is already a two-horse race.
fullText:
Four games is far too soon to be talking about who is in or out of the title race... isn't it?

And yet Arsenal and Manchester City, who have been the top two in three of the past four seasons, look a level above everyone else so far.

Is it already a two-horse race?

With new (or newish) managers, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham were all looking for better things this season.

But so far their starts range from shaky to shambolic.

How Premier League table looks after four games

Arsenal and Manchester City are the only two teams with 12 points from four games.

They are already four points above third-placed Hull City - who despite their brilliant early form may not consider themselves in any kind of title equation - and five above the rest.

Arsenal are the defending champions and pre-season title favourites.

Under manager Mikel Arteta they ended a 22-year title drought last season with what was often perceived to be an attritional style of play.

They started this season with a hugely impressive 3-0 victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield.

And they have carried on with victories over Coventry, Aston Villa, Chelsea and Sunderland - plus Napoli in the Champions League.

Including last season, they are now on a nine-game winning run in the league - and last lost in any competition in 90 minutes to City on 19 April.

Unlike Arsenal, City do not have the continuity this season with boss Pep Guardiola leaving after six titles, including a Treble, in 10 years.

Enzo Maresca, once his assistant, has taken over and led them to four wins from four in the league after that loss in Cardiff to the Gunners.

They have beaten Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Coventry - plus Porto in the Champions League - before their controversial 1-0 success at Manchester United on Sunday.

Erling Haaland scored the only goal, with the Premier League's refereeing body later admitting a mistake as it should have been ruled out for offside.

Despite their 100% starts, the underlying numbers behind Arsenal and City's starts do not imply total dominance.

Brighton (13) and Chelsea (10) have scored more goals than the eight that the top two have both netted.

For shots, Arsenal and City rank 10th and 11th and touches in the opposition box they are sixth and fifth respectively.

Arsenal have only conceded once and City have let in two goals - two of the best records in the league.

Refereeing body admits judgement error over Haaland derby winner

Intelligence & resilience key in statement win for Maresca's Man City - Murphy

'Today the game was unprotected' - Arteta fumes but Arsenal survive

The next three favourites to win the title with most bookmakers - in order - were Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United - with Tottenham some way back.

Chelsea and Liverpool both sacked their managers, bringing in Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola respectively in the summer.

United and Spurs both changed manager earlier in 2026, with Michael Carrick and Roberto de Zerbi having their first pre-seasons.

Last season, Chelsea finished 10th, Liverpool as defending champions were fifth, and Spurs came 17th - with United ending up third after turning things around under Carrick.

So for all four hopes were high this was going to be a better season.

Chelsea are fifth, with only one defeat so far, and have scored 10 goals... but conceded nine - the fourth worst record in the division.

They have conceded two or more goals in each of their first four matches of a Premier League season for the first time since 2015-16.

Liverpool are down in seventh, unbeaten after four games - but three of those are draws.

It is just the third time in the last 63 seasons they have failed to win either of their first two home league games.

United are 13th with four points - equalling their worst start to a Premier League season since 1992-93... level with last season.

They have had more shots than anybody else in the league - 84 - and the second fewest shots conceded (41).

Despite that they have conceded as many as they have scored - seven.

Spurs would not have considered themselves in the title race after two 17th-placed finishes but would have hoped for a better start as they currently sit... 17th.

And even worse than that, it was the first time in the club's history they have failed to score in their first four league games.

Joint-worst start since 1992 and fan protests - Man Utd's day to forget

Toothless Spurs blank again as new era turns into a false dawn

More dropped points at Anfield - is it too early for Liverpool to worry?

New system, same problems - Alonso not happy with 'soft' Chelsea

Prior to this campaign, 80 teams in the English top-flight have won their first four league games of the season.

Of those, just 24 went on to win the title, proving that early dominance does not necessarily mean a side will last the pace.

In the Premier League era, nine of the 28 sides to win four on the bounce at the start of a season have gone on to lift the title, most recently Manchester City in 2023-24.

As the graphic below shows, there have been just six previous Premier League seasons in which two or more teams have won each of their first four fixtures.

And the bad news for the chasing pack is that just two clubs have won the Premier League having been five or more points behind after four games.

Manchester United did it five times under Sir Alex Ferguson (1992-93, 1996-97, 1998-99, 2007-08 and 2008-09), while Pep Guardiola's Manchester City acheived the feat in 2020-21.
